SELECTED_INDEX: 6
CONFIDENCE: 0.35
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by alkyl-group bands:  
• Very strong CH₃/CH₂ rocking at 733 cm⁻¹, typical for branched alkanes.  
• Three strong C–H stretching bands at 2837, 2948 and 2997 cm⁻¹ and a CH₂/CH₃ deformation at 1445 cm⁻¹ correspond to saturated hydrocarbon vibrations.  
• Other observed bands (586, 556, 830, 927, 1083 cm⁻¹) match weaker skeletal C–C modes often seen in highly branched alkanes; no intense C–O (≈1100 cm⁻¹), C–S, S=O or P=O stretches appear, which would be expected for the O-, S- or P-containing candidates.  
The only oxygen- and heteroatom-free option on the list is candidate 6 (CC(C)(C)CC(C)(C)C), a highly branched saturated hydrocarbon, consistent with all observed features.
